title: WPSS/820/2019 of HARI OM Vs BHARAT HEAVY ELECTRICALS LTD.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 820 of 2019
Hari Om Ö Petitioner
Vs
Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. & others Ö Respondents
Mr. D.S. Patni, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Kanti Ram Sharma, learned counsel for
respondents.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Petitioner was an employee of Bharat Heavy
Electricals Ltd. (in short ìBHELî) in its Haridwar Unit, who
retired from service in the month of August, 2016. According to
the petitioner, his date of birth is 12.01.1963; however, the
employer had incorrectly recorded his date of birth as
03.08.1956. In support of this contention, petitioner has relied
upon certain educational certificates, including marksheet and
certificate of 8th Standard, where his date of birth is indicated
as 12.01.1963.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in
the Employeesí State Insurance Corporation record maintained
by ESIC Authorities, petitionerís date of birth is recorded as
12.01.1963. Similarly, in the health identification card issued
by the respondents also, his date of birth is recorded as
12.01.1963.
3. Per contra, Mr. V.K. Kohli, learned Senior Counsel,
appearing for the respondents/BHEL, submits that petitioner
himself had furnished the information in the Enrollment Form,
which was filled by him at the time of his joining in BHEL, in
which he had mentioned his date of birth as 03.08.1956. Mr.
Kohli, further points out that petitioner had passed 8th
examination, after joining service in the year 1990, in which he
had changed his date of birth, therefore, the same cannot be
accepted.
4. It is settled position in law that correction of date of
birth cannot be permitted at the fag end of service career.

2
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to entertain this petition,
however, this Court is of the opinion that ends of justice would
be met, if petitioner is permitted to make representation to the
Competent Authority in BHEL, who shall examine the claim of
the petitioner and take appropriate decision.
5. Accordingly, writ petition is disposed with liberty to
the petitioner to make representation to the Competent
Authority i.e. respondent No. 3 /General Manager, BHEL,
within two weeks from today. If such representation is made,
Competent Authority shall consider the same and take
appropriate decision, in accordance with law, within eight
weeks from the date of receipt of such representation along
with certified copy of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
08.04.2019
Aswal
